paragraphs: Swamiji held that most of the misery we suffer is misery we choose. To show it, he told of an old man in China who had spent sixty years locked in prison.

When a new emperor was crowned, prisoners were released, and the old man was finally let out. But the moment he stepped outside, he cried that he couldn't go on living like this. He couldn't stand the light. He wanted his dreadful dungeon back, with its rats and mice. Kill me, he pleaded, or return me to my cell. And so they sent him back.

We are all exactly like him, said Swamiji. We rush straight towards every kind of suffering and don't really want to be freed from it. Day after day we chase pleasure, and just when we are about to grab it, it slips through our fingers and is gone.
And still we don't stop. On and on we go, chasing the same thing, blind to what we are doing.
learn: People can get so used to what holds them back, whether a habit, a comfort zone or a toxic pattern, that freedom feels frightening. Growth often means putting up with the 'bright light' of change for a while. Notice which cells you keep walking back into.
